To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the National Mental Health Program in India has been implemented with a focus on psychopharmacology, 2) the program has not been successful in achieving its goals of community participation or accessible services, 3) the program's goals have been undermined by the local meanings that the community gives to psychotropic medication, 4) the community's meaning of psychotropic medication is influenced by local cultural beliefs and practices, and 5) the community's understanding of psychotropic medication differs from
psychotropic pills are a powerful symbol of the NMHP and that the pill's meaning changes as it travels from the centre to local communities.

The journey of psychotropic drugs from the central government to the periphery is an important part of understanding how community participation is enacted in a Community Mental Health (CMH) program in northern India.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social, political, economic, and cultural processes that shape the use of psychiatric drugs in the community mental health setting.
how the pill is used as a tool to re-enforce the power of psychiatrists, to re-enforce existing barriers to care and to silence community voices.
the biosocial journey and symbolic inscription of psychotropic pills within India's National Mental health program (NMHP).

the NMHP is a program that is not being implemented.
the NMHP has failed to deliver on its promise of community participation, accessibility and equity.
the pill is a symbol that is both powerful and fragile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NMHP is an example of a policy that was developed without sufficient attention to the local context.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the pill's journey is not only a biosocial one, but also a political one that can be understood only in relation to local cultural contexts.
the pill is not just a pharmacological object but is a powerful symbol that carries multiple meanings and has the ability to shape and reshape social relationships and social structures.
the pill, as an object of policy, is a potent symbol for mental health care.
